signature.name: Cristo Rey
signature.detail: The towering hilltop statue of Christ is Cali's most recognizable sight, offering sweeping views over the city and the Cauca valley. It is a short drive or hike up from the west side of town; go in the late afternoon for cooler air and sunset light, and bring water if you walk up.

signature.name: Cerro de las Tres Cruces
signature.detail: Three crosses crown this hill and mark one of Cali's favorite viewpoints and exercise spots. Locals hike up early in the morning for safety and cooler temperatures; go with others and avoid carrying valuables.

signature.name: San Antonio
signature.detail: This historic old-town neighborhood is known for its colonial charm, bohemian cafés and a small hilltop church with city views. Wander the steep streets in the morning or early evening, and note that the area is best explored on foot.

signature.name: Museo del Oro
signature.detail: Cali's gold museum displays pre-Columbian metalwork and archaeological pieces from the region. It is a compact, affordable indoor stop, ideal for a rainy afternoon; check opening hours before you go.

signature.name: La Merced
signature.detail: A historic religious complex with colonial architecture and a quiet atmosphere in the city center. It pairs well with a walk through the surrounding old streets; dress modestly if you enter the church.

signature.name: Zoológico de Cali
signature.detail: One of Colombia's best-known zoos, home to a wide range of Andean and tropical species. It is a good family half-day out; go early to avoid the midday heat and allow a few hours.

transport: Bus or MIO card around $0.70 a ride; taxis and ride-hailing cheap
